card.one_sentence_claim: Defining macro distance as minimal protocol cost with edge cost = -log(Phat+eta), an isotropic lazy random walk on a torus under increasing staging tau drives the negative-log displacement cost toward a separable quadratic (Pythagorean/Euclidean) form via the CLT, while an L1 control does not - a computational demonstration (not a theorem) that Euclidean metric structure can emerge as a stable P6 accounting law, with curvature read off as loop holonomy.
card.target_known_fact: Under repeated isotropic diffusion the CLT makes displacement distributions approximately Gaussian, so the negative-log transition probability (a natural cost/action) becomes approximately quadratic and separable, giving the Pythagorean/Euclidean (L2) metric rather than L1; this is the discrete shadow of the Onsager-Machlup action and of Varadhan's short-time heat-kernel asymptotics (-2t log p_t -> d^2), and underlies diffusion-map geometry (Coifman-Lafon). Curvature appears as loop holonomy.
card.scientific_domain: Statistical mechanics / emergent geometry / information physics (finite-state Markov dynamics; manifold learning / diffusion geometry)
card.argument_family: low-energy-limit (staging tau -> large is the 'low-energy'/long-time diffusive limit; the metric is the emergent normal form of accounting cost in that limit)
card.minimum_viable_result: A reproducible computational demonstration (already essentially in-paper) that, for a single isotropic torus random walk, defining cost = -log p_tau makes the Pythagorean residual collapse toward zero and cost contours circularize as tau grows, while an L1 control does not - i.e. Euclidean (L2) metric structure emerges as a stable P6 accounting law in the isotropic staged-diffusion regime, with the Gaussian/CLT input explicitly imported. This recovers (does not derive) the standard 'diffusive cost is quadratic => L2 geometry' fact and reorganizes it as an audited closure artifact.
data_matched: Pythagorean residual collapse: median |R_tau| 33.19 (tau=4) -> 0.0586 (tau=128); quadratic-fit RMS 12.10 -> 0.1509; regime transition near tau ~ 16 (pythagoras_rw_grid_summary.json; To_Plot line 504, 598).
Axis-scaling at tau=128: quadratic-axis RMS small vs linear-axis RMS large (cost grows quadratically, not linearly, in displacement).
L1 negative control: diamond-shaped contours, near-zero axis-linear RMS by construction, quadratic-axis fit poor, no residual collapse (To_Plot line 612-623).
Curvature companion (holonomy_demo_summary.json): median loop-holonomy 0.0479 (plane-like grid) vs 0.5980 (sphere-like) over 791 vs 800 loops; median ratio ~12.49 (To_Plot line 559).
Qualitative match to standard diffusive geometry: isotropic-Gaussian heat kernel => circular (L2) level sets, the textbook expectation (no novel empirical data; all synthetic/controlled substrates).
card.baseline_comparison: RECOVERY, not improvement, at the load-bearing step. The standard account (CLT => Gaussian heat kernel => -log p quadratic => L2/Euclidean cost) already explains why diffusive transport cost is quadratic and Euclidean rather than L1. SBT does NOT derive the Gaussian/CLT step - it imports it (cited Durrett2019Probability, To_Plot line 574) - and adds only an audit/closure layer that reframes the result ('distance is accounting (P6)', Pythagoras as a stable closure fixed point, curvature as P3 holonomy). Value-add is methodological: a reproducible, falsification-first, audit-attached demonstration with a Lean-anchored triangle inequality / separation quotient and an explicit (definitional) negative control, not a new physical or mathematical result.
card.honest_status_note: Derivability class C: stylized COMPUTATIONAL DEMONSTRATION, not a derivation. Load-bearing step (CLT => approximately Gaussian displacement => -log p quadratic) is IMPORTED from standard probability (cited Durrett). Only triangle inequality and separation-quotient are Lean-anchored; the quadratic emergence is a finite-tau empirical trend with NO convergence theorem (continuum interface explicitly disclaimed, ledger F43). Varadhan is NOT cited in To_Plot (verified: zero hits) - interpretive overlay added by the atlas builder. Onsager-Machlup also absent from To_Plot (verified). Acknowledged circularity: Euclidean structure partly injected by the isotropic substrate (ledger line 206). L1 control is definitional, not a matched dynamical control (To_Plot line 618). Holonomy explicitly NOT a curvature-tensor certificate (To_Plot line 559). Honors SBT disclaimers.

free_parameters: Staging / lens tau (limit is tau large; regime transition near tau ~ 16; too-large tau inflates prototype drift)
Cost-to-distance convention: cost = -log(Phat+eta) and the eta log-regularizer / edge thresholds
Substrate geometry / isotropy declared externally (torus RW = flat; sphere-like kNN graph = curved; anisotropic gating = deformed)
Torus size N and displacement window (finite-size aliasing failure mode)
Holonomy neighborhood parameters (k_neigh, overlap thresholds, neighborhood expansion)
Prototype / lift U choice and refinement-ladder depth (E5 bypasses the lens ladder, measuring displacement likelihood directly)
auxiliary_assumptions: Substrate diffusion is isotropic and homogeneous; anisotropy/constraints deform the metric (E4), so Euclidean form is conditional on declared isotropy.
Cost is defined as -log transition probability (a specific, non-unique accounting convention); a different convention need not yield L2.
Staging pushes the substrate into a clean Gaussian/CLT diffusion regime; the Gaussian heat kernel and the -log p ~ quadratic step are IMPORTED (cited Durrett), not produced.
Finite-state substrate throughout; quadratic/Pythagorean form is a finite-tau empirical trend, not a proven continuum limit.
Displacement window stays inside the non-aliased support of the torus (N >> diffusion length).
The L1 comparison is a definitional (geometric) control, not a matched dynamical alternative.

audit.opposite_world_explanation: The same pipeline 'retrodicts' the opposite geometry by changing one declared input: anisotropic gating (E4) deforms the metric off-Euclidean; the L1 control is itself a faithfully rendered diamond (non-Euclidean) answer; a sphere-like kNN graph flips holonomy 0.0479->0.5980; a too-small torus vs tau stalls emergence entirely. Substrate-in/geometry-out renderer; the Euclidean answer is selected by choosing an isotropic flat substrate plus the -log-Gaussian convention (ledger line 206).
audit.audit_verdict: FLEXIBILITY HIGH / overfitting risk HIGH, but HONESTLY DISCLOSED. Class-C computational demonstration that RECOVERS (does not derive) the textbook fact that diffusive transport cost is quadratic, hence Euclidean (L2) rather than L1, with a flat-vs-curved holonomy companion. ~10 effective DoF against ~2 qualitative self-generated targets. Load-bearing CLT step imported (Durrett). Only triangle inequality + separation quotient Lean-anchored; Pythagoras emergence itself is NOT Lean-certified (To_Plot line 628 explicitly: 'does not claim Euclidean geometry is fundamental'). Opposite-world fails cleanly. Target-designed end to end. Varadhan/Onsager-Machlup are atlas overlay, absent from To_Plot (verified by grep). No SBT disclaimer crossed. A falsification-first reskin of known diffusive geometry as a P6 idempotent-packaging artifact; methodologically clean, honestly bounded, scientifically a RECOVERY with high definitional flexibility and zero novel content at the load-bearing step.

score_rationale.impact: 2 - A clean conceptual bridge between finite Markov dynamics, diffusion-map geometry and emergent-geometry programs, but it recovers a textbook fact; no new physics or mathematics at the load-bearing step.
score_rationale.execution_ease: 5 - Already in-paper and reproducible from committed configs (pythagoras_rw_grid.yaml, holonomy_demo.yaml); the easy lemma is hours of algebra.
score_rationale.plausibility: 5 - The recovered fact (diffusive cost is quadratic => L2) is textbook-certain; the demonstration reproduces the expected numbers.
score_rationale.non_ad_hocness: 2 - The -log cost convention, the axis-aligned Pythagorean-residual functional, and the isotropic flat substrate are all chosen to produce the target; diagnostic tuned to the expected separable-quadratic form. Lean anchoring of triangle inequality + separation quotient earns partial credit.
score_rationale.discriminative_power: 1 - Opposite-world fails cleanly: the same pipeline renders anisotropic/diamond/curved/stalled outcomes; the negative control is definitional, not dynamical; cannot predict which geometry obtains.
score_rationale.audience_legibility: 4 - Falsification-first, audit-attached, runnable-from-config, with explicit failure modes and honest disclaimers; legible to multiple communities.
score_rationale.precision: 2 - Quantitative in-paper (33.19 -> 0.0586, transition ~tau 16) but no fixed pass/fail threshold, no convergence theorem, no metric tensor; precision capped by SBT's disclaimed continuum interface (F43).
score_rationale.robustness: 2 - Documented failure modes (finite-size aliasing, over-staging drift, neighborhood-sensitive holonomy) and frame-dependence make the result regime-fragile; the headline holds only in a hand-selected window.
score_rationale.baseline_advantage: 1 - Explicitly RECOVERY, not improvement; does worse than the standard account on rigor (Varadhan gives a theorem where SBT gives only a finite-tau trend). Capped low.
score_rationale.publication_potential: 3 - Publishable as a methods/pedagogical note or workshop exhibit on auditable emergent-geometry pipelines, with honest framing; not a results paper for a physics or math venue given zero novel content at the load-bearing step.

triage.bin_rationale: Conceptual reframing: the genuine contribution is methodological/pedagogical - reframing Pythagoras/L2 as a P6 'distance is accounting' closure artifact with a Lean-anchored metric core and an explicit (currently definitional) falsifier. It is not a quick novel win (A), not a foundational sanity check of SBT internals (B), not a flagship result (C - it recovers, does not derive), and not a high-risk numerical bet (D - the numerics already exist and are inexpensive). The only path to genuine novelty (a discrete-Varadhan continuum theorem) is exactly SBT's disclaimed missing interface (F43) and would be high-risk new mathematics, not this exhibit.
triage.recommended_artifact: A self-contained reproducible note: (1) the E5 torus-RW pipeline reproducing the residual-collapse table (33.19->0.0586) and the L1 control, plus the holonomy plane-vs-sphere separation, from committed configs; (2) the short rigorous downstream-of-CLT lemma (isotropic Gaussian displacement => R_tau->0 + circular contours; L1 => diamond); (3) explicit honest framing that the Gaussian step is imported (Durrett), Varadhan/Onsager are not SBT content, the abstract verb is 'recovers' not 'derives', Lean credit is triangle inequality + separation quotient only, and the Euclidean outcome is conditional on the declared isotropic flat substrate. Cheap value-add: add a matched DYNAMICAL (anisotropic/driven) control to upgrade the falsifier from definitional to dynamical.
